planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in spring once soil has warmed, in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Summerwine produces flat-topped clusters of deep wine-red flowers that hold their rich color longer than many pink-toned yarrow cultivars before fading to dusty rose. Plant in lean, fast-draining soil in full sun; rich or wet soil encourages floppy growth and crown rot, especially in humid climates. Deadhead spent flower heads to prolong bloom from early summer into fall, and divide crowded clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor. Established plants are highly drought-tolerant and attract bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in lean, well-drained soil; part of the Seduction series bred for compact habit and vivid, long-lasting color.

directions: Saucy Seduction is a compact Seduction-series selection with saturated magenta-pink flower heads that resist the fading common in older yarrow cultivars, staying vivid for weeks before mellowing slightly with age. Grow in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun, since fertile or damp conditions promote weak, sprawling stems and crown rot. Shear back spent blooms to encourage rebloom through summer, and divide every two to three years to keep clumps vigorous and tidy. Its dense, ferny gray-green foliage stays attractive between bloom flushes and tolerates heat and drought once established.

common_name: Pomegranate Yarrow (Deep Red Summer Series Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or transplants in spring in lean, very well-drained soil; part of the Summer-series breeding line selected for rich, saturated flower color on compact plants.

directions: Pomegranate bears dense, flat-topped flower heads in a deep, saturated red reminiscent of ripe pomegranate arils, aging gradually to a dusky rose rather than washing out to pastel like many older red yarrow selections. It needs lean, sharply drained soil and full sun to stay upright and compact; overly rich soil leads to floppy stems and reduced flower color intensity. Deadhead regularly to keep the long summer bloom season going, and lift and divide congested clumps every few years in spring. Once established it shrugs off heat, drought, and poor soil, making it a low-maintenance choice for pollinator and cutting gardens.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

common_name: Cloth of Gold Yarrow (Tall Golden Fernleaf Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in lean, well-drained soil; stake in exposed sites since this tall selection can lean under wind or heavy rain.

directions: Cloth of Gold is one of the tallest garden yarrow selections, sending up sturdy stems topped with large, flat, brilliant mustard-gold flower heads well above ferny, aromatic gray-green foliage. Plant in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; excessive fertility or moisture produces weaker stems prone to flopping despite the plant's naturally upright habit. It excels at the back of a sunny border or in a cutting garden, since the long-lasting flower heads dry well and hold their gold color for months. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to renew vigor and maintain strong flowering.
